body.p: The old man of garbage. The Khanty people lived in a small town on a large river. One day, fall came, it snowed, and the hunters set off in their sledges. Once upon a time there was a mighty Chante who lived. He also loaded his things into the sled, he had a hunting lodge in the forest, he goes to the hunting lodge. He went to this hunting lodge and started hunting in it. That's how he got to the hunting lodge. So he lives in a hunting lodge all the time. He goes hunting, kills animals: sables, squirrels - all kinds of animals. One day he came home after slaughtering the animals, lay down in bed and put his coat on his legs to keep them warm. He has also put on his Malitsa. It just lies there. It is slowly getting dark. Suddenly someone opened the door and looked over - what' s going on? Grandma Menk came into the house. And she began to approach him, began to examine him: "Kylyo-o," she said, "when he came back from the hunt recently, he only had one head. And now it has become what it has become again. What a miracle! It now has two heads. Which way should I swing the axe now? Which way is his head facing?" And next to him was his axe. While she was stomping around like that, [the Chante] hit the grandmother between the shoulder blades with an axe. He hit her, not her him. The grandmother ran outside with a noise. And he ran after this grandmother. As it turned out, there was a large pile of garbage not far away. The grandmother climbed noisily onto the garbage heap. There was waste that he poured out in winter. He looked down and there was a large house below. The grandmother screams and shouts. It turned out that she had a daughter. And he says to his daughter: "The grandfather who lives on the edge of the houses, [on the edge] of the city, the grandfather shaman will have to be sought out. I'll probably die soon, that's what the Khanty did to me, they hit me with an axe." He hid and her daughter jumped out and ran down the street. A short time later, a tall old man brought her, leading her by the hand and holding his tambourine. She took him home with her. [The Chante] approached the hole again, he looks, it is light in the house. The old man began to shamanize and beat on his large tambourine. Here is a stop. Grandmother Menk said: "And why are you touching this Chante, a Chante who lived alone, a Chante who meant no harm? Let him hunt. Don't you live in the house he built now? If it weren't for these Chants or Nenets who throw away the garbage, what kind of house would we live in?" The old man hammered on his tambourine again, and the axe wound that had been inflicted on the Chante healed before her grandmother's eyes. Grandma is feeling a little better. So she says to her daughter: "Take this grandfather back". This is the grandfather she brought back. And he [the Chante] lay face down again on the floor next to the door. There's that girl again. And then he caught her. Let's fight, if he wins he drags them outside his door, if the Menk girl wins they end up back near the trash heap. They fight, fight, finally it dawns, the dawn begins to appear. In the end, the girl said, "You're stronger than me anyway, I'll come myself since you're wooing me." Then he let her go, [she] went home, [and he] went hunting again. Hunt, hunt, hunt. One day I came home after hunting, in the evening I went into the house and there was a girl sitting there. And they began to live there together. They lived short or they lived long. And he had forgotten his city. All the time, even in summer, they lived in his house all the time and started living from that moment on. And one day, while they were living like this, a boy was born to them. That's how long they live. While hunting and killing various animals, his wife once said: "Just shake the snow off your skis. When you arrive, you stomp your skis [with a stick], shake the snow off them. One day he went hunting again. He came home in the evening and thought: "Why do I have to walk on skis and shake off the snow? She is probably with another man. I'm going to put my skis down slowly now." The woman's heart lungs popped out of her mouth and the baby in the cradle died in the cradle. That's it. What can you do? Where would he take them, he took them to the garbage heap, he took them closer to his garbage, he probably buried them there somewhere. He will no longer sit in an empty house all the time like he used to, he has gone back to his city. He's still alive now, it seems. And that was it.
